stem: A practitioner appropriately treats opioid use disorder with a Schedule III narcotic medication that may lawfully be prescribed for maintenance or detoxification treatment. Which statement best distinguishes this from Schedule II methadone maintenance?

choices.text: Qualifying Schedule III-V narcotic OUD drugs use a prescription pathway under applicable law; methadone maintenance follows a different federal framework.
A Schedule III narcotic used for OUD is reclassified as Schedule II for the duration of treatment.
Schedule III narcotic OUD therapy must be dispensed through the same OTP pathway used for methadone maintenance.
The first OUD dose converts the Schedule III medication to noncontrolled status for later outpatient fills.
The federal OUD rule gives pharmacists independent prescribing authority for qualifying Schedule III-V narcotics.

explanation.core_reasoning: Qualifying Schedule III-V narcotic OUD medications have a prescription pathway that differs materially from routine Schedule II methadone maintenance rules.

choice_analysis.A: Federal law distinguishes the qualifying Schedule III-V prescription pathway from methadone maintenance.
choice_analysis.B: Indication does not reclassify a Schedule III drug.
choice_analysis.C: The federal framework distinguishes qualifying Schedule III-V prescribing from methadone maintenance.
choice_analysis.D: Treatment does not remove the drug's federal controlled status.
choice_analysis.E: The treatment rule does not independently create pharmacist prescriptive authority.

related_facts: State scope and all other prescribing requirements still apply.
explanation.mpje_trap: Applying methadone's Schedule II pathway to every OUD medication.

reasoning_steps: Identify the drug as Schedule III-V narcotic treatment
Distinguish its federal OUD pathway from Schedule II methadone maintenance
